solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Remote is damaged, that's irritating

indicators.note: something damaged has been knocked out of shape, so the letters before it are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; it doubles as part of the anagram signal phrase

explanation.surface: Someone finds their broken TV remote infuriating.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'is' does double duty: its letters join the fodder while 'is damaged' reads as the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tiresome is tedious and annoying, a close synonym of irritating.

clue.text: Check start of plumber's progress — one'll protect the home

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: to dam is to check or hold back a flow
the opening letter of plumber's
a course is a progression or onward movement

explanation.surface: A plumber's progress is held up while the householder is reassured.
explanation.walkthrough: A damp course is the waterproof layer laid in a wall near the ground to stop moisture rising into a house.
explanation.definitionFit: The waterproof barrier in a wall protects a house from rising damp, hence one that protects the home.

clue.text: Until now the roe let out warning call

indicators.note: a garment let out is altered and reshaped, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
golfers shout fore to warn of a flying ball

explanation.surface: A fish's roe is released while a warning cry rings out.
explanation.definitionFit: Heretofore is a formal adverb meaning before this time, the same as until now.

clue.text: Riches flunkey picked up

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting something up turns the word to read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a tool is a person used by another, a lackey

explanation.surface: A servant lifts some treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' looks like a sound clue (a lute is plucked), but it is a reversal in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Loot is informal for money or wealth, so it stands for riches.

clue.text: Reverse spin gets a sideways glance

indicators.note: to reverse something is to turn it backwards, so the word is read from its end

blocks.note: to reel is to whirl or spin round

explanation.surface: Putting backspin on a ball earns a sly look from an opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: A leer is a sly, lascivious look cast out of the corner of the eye.

clue.text: Spoil second vehicle

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for second
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone damages their second car.
explanation.definitionFit: To scar is to mark or disfigure, which is to spoil the look of something.

clue.text: Steamship seen in blooming trouble

indicators.note: something seen in another sits inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: blooming with health is hale
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: A steamship runs into some flaming bother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blooming' reads as a mild British swearword, but it means healthy here.
explanation.definitionFit: Hassle is informal for bother, annoyance or difficulty.

clue.text: Face travel document, say, being returned

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the short word is read backwards

blocks.note: a visa is an entry permit stamped in a passport
e.g. means for example, which is what say means here

explanation.surface: A traveller is told to show their document as it is handed back.
explanation.definitionFit: Visage is a literary word for a person's face or expression.

clue.text: Raglan perhaps is done with cold cereal

blocks.note: something over is finished
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
oat is a cereal grain

explanation.surface: Lord Raglan has finished with his cold porridge.
explanation.walkthrough: A raglan is a coat whose sleeves run up to the collar, named after Lord Raglan; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A raglan is a style of loose overcoat, so it is an example of the answer.

clue.text: Little Penny's sob

blocks.note: wee is Scottish for little
p is the abbreviation for a penny

explanation.surface: A small girl called Penny is crying.
explanation.definitionFit: To sob is to cry noisily, and to weep is to shed tears.

clue.text: Undertaking to go in quietly and go up

blocks.note: to enter is to go in
p is piano, the musical marking for quietly
joins the last two pieces
to rise is to go up

explanation.surface: A burglar's plan: creep in silently and head upstairs.
explanation.definitionFit: An enterprise is a project or venture, something undertaken.

clue.text: Please mimic old fogey — lost old bird that couldn't wing it

definitions.text: lost old bird that couldn't wing it

blocks.note: to do is to suffice or satisfy, as in 'that will do'
to do someone is to impersonate them

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to impersonate a stuffy old person, then an extinct flightless bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Two short pieces build the word, and two definitions follow: a stick-in-the-mud and the extinct flightless bird of Mauritius.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodo is slang for a hopelessly old-fashioned person, and literally the flightless bird wiped out in the 1600s.

clue.text: Oscar writes on English island mostly, one's not well-kept

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the island is dropped

blocks.note: Oscar is O in the phonetic alphabet
to pen is to write
E is the abbreviation for English
Crete is a Greek island

explanation.surface: Oscar Wilde writes about an English island, mostly.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 'one' stands for a secret, so the definition reads as 'a secret that is not well kept'.
explanation.definitionFit: An open secret is supposedly confidential but in fact widely known, so it has not been kept.

clue.text: Plant from perhaps Morecambe area

blocks.note: Eric Morecambe was a famous British comedian, of Morecambe and Wise
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A plant has come from the area around the seaside town of Morecambe.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe looks like the Lancashire resort town, but it is the comedian's surname; 'perhaps' shows Eric is one example of a Morecambe.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is the botanical genus of heaths and heathers, so it names a plant.

clue.text: Cryptic setter's wrong about golf — it gives you a name

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling or obscured, so the following word is jumbled
about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the letter for golf

blocks.note: taken as written
a sin is a wrong
Golf is G in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A puzzle-setter blunders over a golf reference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cryptic setter' reads as the crossword compiler, but cryptic is the anagram signal; the 's attaches the next piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A street sign displays the name of the road, so it gives you a name.

clue.text: What could be of superb quality? Possibly, fancy sweet

blocks.note: 'the cheese' is old slang for the best or the very thing
a fancy is a small iced cake

explanation.surface: A question of whether some fancy dessert might be first-rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like an adjective describing the sweet, but it is a noun: fancies are small decorated cakes. 'The cheese' meaning the top thing is dated British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheesecake is a rich dessert, and a dessert is a sweet in British usage.

clue.text: Name on lug is handy

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for name
places the first piece before the second
lug is informal British for ear

explanation.surface: A name tag on a handle comes in useful.
explanation.definitionFit: Handy can mean close at hand, conveniently nearby, which is a sense of near.

clue.text: Willow is more promising, one right for the chop

indicators.note: something for the chop is about to be cut off, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: a rosier outlook is a more hopeful one
R is the abbreviation for right; one marks a single R

explanation.surface: A willow tree looks healthier, though one on the right is due to be felled.
explanation.walkthrough: The word has two Rs; 'one right' says only one of them goes, the first.
explanation.definitionFit: The osier is a kind of willow whose pliant shoots are used in basketwork.

clue.text: Place lacking in charm gives comfort

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so the abbreviation is taken away from the word that follows

blocks.note: PL is the abbreviation for place in street names
to please is to charm or delight

explanation.surface: A house with no charm still offers some comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: Ease means freedom from pain or worry, a state of comfort.

clue.text: Difficult end brought into being

blocks.note: a stub is the leftover end of a pencil or cigarette
born means brought into existence

explanation.surface: A troublesome finish came about.
explanation.definitionFit: A stubborn person is obstinate and hard to deal with, which makes them difficult.

clue.text: Put one's foot down — a late recce is out of order

indicators.note: things out of order are in the wrong sequence, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written; a recce is a reconnaissance

explanation.surface: A commander insists that a belated scouting mission is unacceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put one's foot down' looks like insisting firmly, but it means pressing the accelerator pedal.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting your foot down on the pedal makes a car go faster, an idiom for speeding up.

clue.text: Conservative bar is bright

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a lever is a rigid bar used to prise

explanation.surface: A Tory drinking spot is said to be smart.
explanation.definitionFit: Bright means intelligent, and clever is a direct synonym in that sense.

clue.text: Complacent son features

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
mug is slang for the face, a person's features

explanation.surface: A self-satisfied son appears in the story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Features' looks like a verb (stars in), but it is the noun for the face.
explanation.definitionFit: Smug means excessively pleased with oneself, the same as complacent.

clue.text: Soft situation in a prickly plot?

definitions.text: Soft situation in a prickly plot?

blocks.note: surface reading: a cushy, comfortable position in life
setter's reading: a garden plot full of thorny flowers, the literal sense of the idiom

explanation.surface: A cosy job turns out to sit inside a thorny scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for an easy, comfortable life literally names a garden bed planted with thorny flowers, which is the prickly plot.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means an easy, pleasant situation, while its literal sense is a garden bed full of thorny shrubs.

clue.text: Look over broken leg

indicators.note: something broken is smashed apart, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over
taken as written, as the fodder

explanation.surface: A doctor examines a fractured leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look over' reads as a phrase meaning examine, but only 'Look' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To ogle is to stare at someone, so it is a kind of look.

clue.text: Sincere in the matter of a Liberal

blocks.note: re means concerning
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A politician claims honesty on a Liberal issue.
explanation.definitionFit: Real feelings are genuine ones, so real can mean sincere.

clue.text: Many turn round

blocks.note: first meaning: a large number, as in a whole lot
second meaning: to swing or skid sideways

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a noun used as 'a large quantity'; the second is a verb for swivelling.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a large quantity as a noun and to swing round on a pivot as a verb.

clue.text: Block what Potter wields, black within

indicators.note: within means inside, so one letter sits in the middle of the other piece

blocks.note: a potter here is a snooker player, who uses a cue
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Harry Potter's wand has a black block inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: Potter looks like Harry Potter or a ceramicist, but it is someone who pots balls at snooker.
explanation.definitionFit: A cube is a solid six-sided block, like a sugar cube or a toy building block.

clue.text: Snitch is utter legend, perhaps

blocks.note: to tell is to utter or say
a legend is one kind of tale

explanation.surface: An informer is declared a total legend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' reads as an adjective meaning complete, but it is the verb to say.
explanation.definitionFit: A telltale is someone who reports others' wrongdoing, which is what a snitch does.

clue.text: Good and satisfactory design for racer

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
joins the pieces
OK means satisfactory
design is a form of art

explanation.surface: A decent, acceptable design for a racing car.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-kart is a small low open vehicle used in kart racing.
